fact_text: Yango describes itself as a technology platform and marketplace that matches riders with independent drivers, and says it owns neither the vehicles nor the drivers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's group is headquartered in the UAE and runs its app, dispatch and mapping on in-house technology built globally, which the Pakistan team adapted locally.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango uses its own map service rather than paying Google Maps for each dispatch, which the interviewee said helps keep its cost base low enough for sustainable fares.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said Yango operates in Africa, Europe, Latin America, Central Asia, the UAE and Asia, and called Pakistan one of its fastest-growing markets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango entered Pakistan around June to July 2023 with a large launch, starting in Lahore, according to the reporter's recollection, and the interviewee said the launch was hard given the economic and political climate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee is Yango's country head for Pakistan, as the host introduced the interview.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's safety centre lets a rider add trusted contacts once, who then receive trip details and can track the ride, so contacts need not be re-entered for each trip.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's app has an SOS button linked to an emergency number, and the interviewee said she tested it herself; the company is working to connect more authorities to the app.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango provides insurance covering both riders and drivers, and the company bears that cost itself, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango runs support around the clock; requests are tagged urgent or non-urgent, and staff make an outbound call when a serious case comes in.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango verifies both drivers and vehicles through a document check that must be passed before a driver can go live on the platform.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango works with Safe City Islamabad: verified drivers and cars carry a QR code that the city scans in real time, and Yango hopes to extend the arrangement to other cities.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said full driver and vehicle verification across all cities cannot be achieved overnight, so the safety rollout is still a work in progress.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango runs a Max mode for full-time drivers and a Flex mode for part-time drivers such as students and salaried workers who cannot commit a full working day.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango launched its Flex mode in Karachi in about November 2025, and the interviewee said early adoption has been strong.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said Yango's driver base includes women, some of whom are the main earners of their families, and that Flex mode suits people who cannot drive a full day.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's driver network runs through transport partners who manage groups of drivers in each city, and a driver can bring a community of other drivers onto the platform.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee cited drivers who moved from bikes to rickshaws and then to cars, one of whom paid a car down payment after about 1.5 years on the platform, as proof that drivers can become business owners.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee called drivers the backbone of a ride-hailing business, so retention depends on driver earnings, dispatch quality, app experience and support.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said Yango's aim is to maximise gross merchandise value per user through repeat use rather than higher prices, a metric she compared with average revenue per user in telecoms.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's stated Pakistan plan is to build a true super app by adding several services on top of ride-hailing, which the interviewee said no local player has yet achieved.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: As of the interview date, the interviewee said Yango's Pakistan operation had been profitable for about two to three years, and that low fares are sustained by cost discipline rather than discounts.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: In an illustration, the interviewee said Yango keeps about PKR 100 from a PKR 1,500 ride and argued that the platform earns from frequency of use rather than from a higher price per ride.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango runs a driver competition with more than 100 prizes, including a car, awarded to drivers who consistently qualify in their city.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's Driver Dreams programme, launched in 2024, lets drivers submit a personal goal such as a house or a relative's healthcare, and the company has helped about 10 drivers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango rewards high-performing drivers with Umrah trips, and the interviewee cited a driver who won a ticket and was offered sponsorship for a family member as well.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Ride-hailing pricing follows demand and supply: when driver supply falls below demand, fares rise, and when supply exceeds demand, fares fall, the basic economic logic the interviewee described.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: A ride fare must cover fuel, vehicle maintenance, platform costs and taxes, plus the driver's margin, so a fare below these operating costs cannot be sustained.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee argued that a ride which can be priced at PKR 500 should not be priced at PKR 800 to 900, since fair pricing keeps both driver income and rider affordability.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Surge (peak) fares rise with the imbalance between demand and driver supply; the interviewee said a 20% imbalance triggers a proportionate factor, and a larger gap triggers a higher peak.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Ride-hailing platforms run surge and anti-surge pricing several times in a day, and Yango sets these automatically by a pricing system rather than by hand, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: A regular non-AC car ride in Pakistan costs roughly PKR 300 to 500, varying by city and demand, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Booking a ride in the app takes about 15 seconds and shows the driver's arrival time, whereas the old way of hailing and haggling over a taxi took the rider at least three times as long.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Earnings per trip are lower for bike riders than for car drivers because the average bike fare is smaller, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee bought a car in 2021 and sold it in December 2023 for 1.5 times the purchase price, despite normal depreciation, which was cited as a sign of how vehicle values moved in the period.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said heavy investment around 2015 to 2016 flooded ride-hailing with capital, and that this investment built the vehicle supply the market has relied on since.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Several ride-hailing businesses exited Pakistan around 2022, which the interviewee said shook investor faith in the sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said ride-hailing in Pakistan has low barriers to entry, so well-funded players can enter and push for share, which means the industry is not yet mature.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said earlier ride-hailing players in Pakistan relied on heavy discounts, rider and driver bonuses and investor-funded guarantees, a model she said cannot be sustained once prices return to normal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Yango's management said discount-led customer stickiness is not real loyalty, so the company sets fares at a sustainable level and relies on repeat use.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said it is unfair for investors to expect a heavily loss-making ride-hailing business to reach break-even overnight, since development takes time.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Drivers complained to Yango that they receive more rides than they want; the interviewee called this a sign of success and said the company invests in tactical interventions to balance it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewer cited a PKR 40,000 minimum wage and said Yango's top captains earn three to four times that amount, a claim the company promotes on billboards.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: Pakistan has a very large population with little formal public transport, so point-to-point demand is strong, and the interviewee said this basic need is one government should meet.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan lacks a ride-hailing regulatory framework covering licensing, insurance rules, taxi categories and bank leasing for vehicles, which keeps the market immature.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan's large population makes it attractive for growth, but economic and political instability weighs on investor confidence and on how businesses enter the market.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Roadmap Behind Yango's Market Takeover | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-18)
